title: Ruby Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Print a message
examples.description: puts prints a value and moves to a new line. Quoted letters make a string.

examples.title: Keep a named number
examples.description: Ruby variables give names to values. The plus sign adds numbers.

examples.title: Put a value in text
examples.description: Inside double quotes, #{name} places a value into text.

examples.title: Make a choice
examples.description: if runs a block when its rule is true. Ruby closes this block with end.
examples.code:
score = 8
if score >= 5
  puts "Pass"
else
  puts "Try again"
end

examples.title: Read a list item
examples.description: An array keeps values in order. The first index is zero.

examples.title: Repeat with a block
examples.description: each visits each item. The name between vertical bars is the current item.

examples.title: Write a method
examples.description: A method is a named set of steps. Ruby returns the last expression by default.
examples.code:
def twice(n)
  n * 2
end
puts twice(4)

examples.title: Find a value by label
examples.description: A hash pairs keys with values. :title is a symbol used as a key.
examples.code:
book = { title: "Moon Trip", pages: 24 }
puts book[:title]

examples.title: Change every item
examples.description: map makes a new array from the result of a block for each item.

examples.title: Handle no value
examples.description: nil means no value. The || operator chooses the right side when the left side is nil or false.

examples.title: Make a small object
examples.description: A class groups data and methods. initialize runs when a new object is made.

examples.title: Handle an expected error
examples.description: rescue handles an error of a named kind. Integer tries to read a whole number from text.
examples.code:
begin
  puts Integer("cat")
rescue ArgumentError
  puts "Use a whole number"
end
